chapter: Coming up in New York and Harlem theatres
title: Back at Suntaug Lake Inn, sending trios to Lake George and gambling
summary: After the war he returns to his Boston job, books a trio at Lake George, then works there himself in 1921 and loses his money gambling.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: You came back to New York.

Well, I went to New York -- this was in 1919 when I got back to Boston and I went back to my old job, but that didn't last long, see, at Suntaug Lake Inn, that didn't last long so then meanwhile I was sending guys out to Lake George, our trio, I used to send them out to Lake George every summer.
So you sort of got in the booking business, like, contracting.

Yeah, because I had a good job and I give them the job and they used to come out with $2,400 and all that and here I'm starving. So I went up there the next -- I think in '21 I went up there, Decoration Day they opened, May 30th and they keep open till Labor Day and I stayed out there and I made good money, but you know what, I had to borrow $50 from the boss to come back to Boston and the only thing I had to show for it was a trunk. I bought a trunk. I paid $125 for a trunk.
What did you do with your money up there.

Gambling, yeah, they gambled there, shucks, man, if you could win and I couldn't win and then they give me -- shoot $100 and I'd shoot it for them and fade out and I said aw shucks, every cent I got I used to gamble with. And so finally I got back to Boston and I started working again and Wilbur Sweatman came through.
